side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.3 emit hard_case:community_consensus_protocol_violation:{C}
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.2 // short by signatures alone: held, never refused (CC 3.3.4)
note: The community pseudo-code emits the violation row and rejects as soon as signatures_ok is false; it has no hold arm. The family pseudo-code and CC 3.3.4 hold a change short only of signatures as cosign:pending for the hold window, and CC 3.1.3 calls that hold general to any cosigned row. One implementer refuses a community widening or removal that arrives one signature short and records a violation; the other holds it 72 h. CC 3.3.4, CC 3.1.3 and the cosigned_act policy row support the hold.

side_a: CC 2.6.6.3 such a community admits by invitation and the constraint describes it rather than gates it
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.3 return false // location outside community's geographic bound
note: CC 2.6.6.3 (and the CC 3.2 district row) say a geographic community whose constraint is finer than resolution 7 admits by invitation and its constraint does not gate. evaluate_subkind_admission gates every geographic community on a contained, unexpired location_proof and has no finer-than-7 arm, so under it such a community can admit nobody at all. Part 2 and CC 3.2 support the invitation reading; the pseudo-code is the stale side.

side_a: CC 4.5.4 Belonging to the set holds no duty, so a member who has not been appointed moderates nothing.
side_b: CC 4.5.13 A founder holds the duty at zero hops and no row confers it
note: authority_set(C) is "a founder, or a key the community's consensus_protocol authorizes". The authority-set paragraph of CC 4.5.4 says belonging to it holds no duty; CC 4.5.13 and a later paragraph of CC 4.5.4 ("its zero-hop duty persists") say a founder holds the duty with no row. Read alone, the first refuses a moderation act signed by a founder nobody appointed, and locks the room for election while a founder is live; the second admits the act and never locks. CC 4.5.13 (founder's seat, "A founder is never locked out") supports the zero-hop reading; the authority-set sentence lacks the founder exception.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.3 (same six canonical kinds as family)
side_b: CC 3.2 the family's kinds less founder_only, which a community above the family never names (CC 4.5.13)
note: CC 4.4.3.2.3 gives a community the family's six kinds, founder_only among them; CC 3.2, CC 3.3.4, CC 4.5.12.5 and CC 4.5.13 refuse founder_only for a community above the family. It also omits open:self_admit, which its own public arm reads. The rest of the document supports the CC 3.2 side.

side_a: CC 4.5.4 its zero-hop duty persists when the community moves from `founder_only`
side_b: CC 4.5.13 A community above the family that names it is refused `federation_community_consensus_protocol_violation`
note: CC 4.5.4 speaks of a community that was founded under founder_only and later moves off it; CC 4.5.13 (and CC 3.2) refuse a community that names founder_only, so no community is ever in the state the sentence starts from. The sentence is left over from before the refusal; the founder's zero-hop duty it carries is unaffected.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 `active_count` (owners active in at least one of the last four periods)
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 Owners active within the window, after the ratchet; every member recomputes it, else census_expected_active_mismatch.
note: Still there. CC 3.1.3 and the first sentence of CC 6.1.9 ("the count of owners whose recent bit is set") make active_count the raw count; CC 2.6.1.7 makes it the count after the ratchet, and floor_applied ("Whether the ratchet's floor, not the raw count, set active_count") only makes sense on that reading. Every member recomputes and refuses a differing row, so a publisher on one reading has its row refused by members on the other whenever the ratchet clips. C156 names this as "C156b", and no row C156b exists in the table; the wording in both places is unchanged. The 8.10 card (combine=max(count(owner),(prev*9+9) div 10,floor)) is on the after-the-ratchet side.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 the ballot and the acceptance are the rows of [CC 3.1.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.4)
side_b: CC 3.1.3 **A member's ballot in a moderator election**
note: Citation. ballot:moderator and ballot:moderator_acceptance are registered in the table of CC 3.1.3; CC 3.1.4 is the transport and delivery section and holds no ballot row.

side_a: CC 4.2.1 Emergency relief is threshold-1 on the announce carrier, TTL ≤ 72 h, not renewable back-to-back by the same holder.
side_b: CC 8.10 - [emergency] expiry required `valid_until` max `mesh_config_emergency_ttl_secs` (CC 4.2.1.4, CC 4.2.1, CC 3.1.9.2)
note: The data for mesh_config:{key} (manifests/reactions.json and the CC 8.10 card) carries the 72 h ceiling and the narrow-only fold. Nothing in the card, the guards or the reactions carries "not renewable back-to-back by the same holder", so a door built from the data admits a second emergency row from the same signer the moment the first lapses. The card also names the signer "steward" where CC 4.2.1 and CC 3.1.9.2 say the trust root.

side_a: CC 3.2 With no live *external* trust root, a substrate MUST disable federated agent capabilities and manifest validation, server-tier and fail-closed.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8 With no valid *external* trust root, federated agent capabilities and manifest validation MUST be disabled at the server tier.
note: One rule, two adjectives. CC 3.2 T7 gives "live" a defined meaning for a root (at least M + 1 active founders) against "stalled", and says a stalled root stays valid and a node attached to it stays federated. Read with T7's sense, "no live external trust root" would switch federated capabilities off under a stalled root; CC 4.4.3.8's "valid" and T7/T8 ("no running node loses federation") support valid.

side_a: CC 4.5.1 Before the scale gate the steward MAY set the entrenchment quorum as low as a strict majority of the standing roster.
side_b: CC 4.5.1.2 before the scale gate it is exercised by the steward under the scale gate in [CC 4.5.1](#4.5.1)
note: Still there (C089 is held as the steward's wording). CC 4.5.1.2 already fixes the entrenchment quorum at a strict majority and says the steward exercises the ratification before the gate; CC 4.2.3 adds that before the gate an accord quorum "reaches the steward as a proposal and nothing more". The MAY in CC 4.5.1 reads as if a quorum above a strict majority applied before the gate and the steward could lower it.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.1.1 amendment process routes through `locality:decision:federation` by default
side_b: CC 4.5.1 **Until the mesh reaches scale, amendment authority rests with the founder as steward, and any accord-holder may propose an amendment**
note: CC 4.4.3.1.1 routes every amendment through the federation locality pool and says that pool is sized to hold "always" from genesis; CC 4.5.1 (normative, the home) defers the whole Contribution and quorum machinery to the scale gate and puts the decision with the steward until then. CC 4.5.1 governs; the locality sentence does not say it applies only after the gate.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.1.1 only the HUMANITY_ACCORD CONSTITUTIONAL halt ([CC 4.2](part_4_composition_governance.md)) can resolve it
side_b: CC 4.5.9.1 The halt pauses agents' acts and touches no data door ([CC 4.2.1.1](#4.2.1.1)), so it is not the remedy here
note: CC 4.4.3.1.1 names the constitutional halt as the one thing that resolves an amendment surface whose federation pool has fallen below its minimum. CC 4.2.1.1 (restated at CC 4.5.9.1) makes the halt a pause of agents' acts that reaches no data door and decides nothing, and CC 4.2.1 limits accord powers to a closed list. A halt cannot restore a pool or decide an amendment; what resolves the state is unstated.

side_a: CC 1.15.5 Governance & Oversight: Require authorised review for changes to ethical logic.
side_b: CC 1.16.6 any change to core ethical logic requires WA sign-off.
note: CC 1.16.6 is marked as restating CC 1.15.5 and is narrower in one way and stronger in another: "core" ethical logic only, and a Wise Authority sign-off where the home asks for an authorised review by an unnamed reviewer. Neither names the row or seat. CC 4.3 and CC 7.3.3 (WA sign-off at Tier 5) lean to the WA.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3 **on behalf of a delegator that itself holds licence authority** by quorum
side_b: CC 2.4.1.2.1 There is no roster of permitted authorities and a substrate checks none.
note: C218 is settled for CC 2.4.1.2.1, whose provenance sentence now reads "Where the authority is a collective it is constituted by quorum". The same unqualified "by quorum" is still in the `license` row of the CC 4.4.3.4.3 scope table, beside its own "Anyone may be an authority under their own key". A single-key authority holds licence authority with no quorum; the table cell still reads as if quorum conferred it.

side_a: CC 5.3.6.1 `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds-until-reset epoch)
side_b: CC 5.3.6.1 `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds-until-reset epoch)
note: One statement that reads two ways: a count of seconds until the reset, or an epoch timestamp of the reset. A server on one reading and a client on the other wait the wrong time. No other statement or data settles it (both sides are the same phrase).

side_a: CC 4.5.13 A client renders an item with no node, from the data alone.
side_b: CC 4.5.13 **Every string the client shows is served by the node as a text reference,**
note: With no node reads as "without a node", which the next paragraphs deny: the client renders two node-served shapes and holds no copy of any string. The sentence closes a paragraph on items answered before the node is claimed, so it probably means an unclaimed node or "no code particular to the item"; as written a reader may build a client that renders offline from held data.

side_a: CC 3.3.9 latest `asserted_at`, tie-break smallest `attestation_id`
side_b: CC 5.3.2.3 Then the `MergeBallot` comparator: `quorum_weight` → signed timestamp → content hash.
note: Two orders for the current state of one licence on its stable id. CC 3.3.9 (citing CC 3.5.1): latest asserted_at, then smallest attestation id. CC 5.3.2.3: quorum weight first, then the signed timestamp, then content hash, with the more restrictive state winning a conflict. For two writes of the same revision, a later `active` signed by fewer members beats an earlier `suspended` under CC 3.3.9 and loses under CC 5.3.2.3, so two nodes disagree on whether a person is licensed. The CC 8.10 card carries both picks side by side (key=license_id; pick=max(asserted_at),min(attestation_id) and pick=max(quorum_weight),max(asserted_at),min(content_hash)), so the data does not decide. CC 5.3.2.3 gives its reason (timestamp front-running); CC 3.3.9 is the general CC 3.5.1 rule restated.

side_a: CC 3.1.1 so a consumer composes the set rather than reading a scalar
side_b: CC 5.3.2.3 More-restrictive state wins on conflict: `revoked` > `suspended` > `active`.
note: CC 3.1.1 keeps concurrent statuses as a set (its canonical vocabulary is issued, probation, restricted, suspended, revoked, lapsed, surrendered, reduced; "active" is not in it). CC 5.3.2.3 ranks three states and keeps one, and uses `active`, as CC 3.3.9 does. A careful reader takes the rank as the merge of two writes of one licence record and the set as the read over status rows, but the text never says so, and the card holds both result=set and pick=rank(revoked>suspended>active).

side_a: CC 3.3.9 `supersedes` to amend, `withdraws` to revoke
side_b: CC 3.1.1 **`suspended` is reversible; `revoked` is terminal**
note: Two ways to revoke a licence. CC 3.3.9 revokes by a `withdraws` of the licence row; CC 3.1.1 and CC 2.4.1.2.1 ("The authority ends those with `suspended` or `revoked`") revoke by a status row, and `revoked` is terminal. The card gives withdraw the way back "attest", so a licence revoked by withdrawal comes back on a fresh attest while one revoked by status cannot (cut=terminal). CC 3.1.1 carries the MUST.

side_a: CC 3.3.7 `capacity:*` carries a substrate-side consent **admission** gate on `consent:scope:analyze`
side_b: CC 3.3.1 is **descriptive** — no fold reads it and it confers nothing
note: Still there. C188 is settled for CC 3.3.1 (the gate reads the `scope` member `analyze` of consent:state:granted; a consent:scope:{kind} dimension row is descriptive) and its resolution says the prose use is repaired. The dimension spelling is still the name of the gate in prose at CC 3.3.7, CC 3.1.4 and CC 3.1.8.1, and in the CC 3.4.5 table row. A door built from those looks for a consent:scope:analyze row and refuses a capacity row whose subject holds the grant CC 3.3.1 means, or admits one on a row CC 3.3.1 says confers nothing.
